articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn Live Press Conference Highlights and Updates
articles.summary: There's nothing like a pre-fight boxing press conference.
articles.body:
Dana White finished his remarks, suggested all the questions were finished, and said the fighters would face off.

Instead, Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn left from opposite sides of the stage and Garcia emptied his pockets of the eggs he'd carried in, and they came back four minutes later, going jaw to jaw after the co-main fighters – Jai Opetaia and Noel Mikaelian – had a brief faceoff.

Garcia continued to chat toward Benn as White stood between then. Benn held an index finger to his mouth in a shushing gesture. But it never got physically contentious and both men were off the stage less than three minutes after arriving.

articles.title: WWE 2K27 Superstar Cover to Be Decided by 1st-Ever Fan Vote, Oba Femi Among 8 Finalists Revealed
articles.summary: Fans can help decide the WWE Superstar that will be featured on the cover of an edition of WWE 2K27.
articles.body:
Fans can help decide the WWE Superstar that will be featured on the cover of an edition of WWE 2K27.

On Thursday, WWE announced the first-ever fan vote for the upcoming video game that allows registered Club WWE members to vote between eight WWE Superstars to appear on a cover.

The eight finalists include Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Fatal Influence, Je'Von Evans, Penta, Sol Ruca, Stephanie Vaquer and Trick Williams.

Fan voting through the Club WWE platform begins on Friday.

CM Punk was previously featured on the Standard Edition cover of WWE 2K26, while Triple H was on the cover for the Kings of Kings Edition of the last game.

WWE 2K26 also contained an Attitude Era Edition as well as a Monday Night War Edition, with both covers featuring an array of wrestling legends.

For the new game, Femi could continue his ascent since making his main roster debut in Dec. 2025 by getting voted to appear on a cover.

He previously took down Brock Lesnar in their Hell in a Cell clash at SummerSlam to conclude their trilogy of matches.

The 28-year-old also defeated Bron Breakker at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event, although it was a disqualification victory after Bronson Reed made his return to help Breakker beat down Femi after the final result.

As for WWE 2K27, the release date of the video game has yet to be revealed.

articles.title: WWE star Nattie explains in-ring character amid Ronda Rousey comparisons, would entertain MMA bout
articles.summary: Nattie says her WWE character comes from Stu Hart's Dungeon, not Ronda Rousey, as she prepares for AAA Triplemania 34 in Las Vegas.
articles.body: WWE star Nattie Neidhart, known simply as Nattie, pushed back on comparisons between her current in-ring character and that of Ronda Rousey when she was performing for the company. Neidhart spoke ahead of her fatal four-way match at AAA’s Triplemania 34 Night 1 in which she will compete for the No. 1 contender spot for the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship. With UFC and Zuffa Boxing hosting events in Las Vegas on the same weekend, OutKick Dropkick asked her if she would entertain a mixed martial arts match. First, Rousey was on her mind. COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK "It’s funny because this headline that’s been going around all day. It says, ‘Natalya’s character is nothing like Ronda Rousey,’ and I was laughing about that because somebody had compared me to Ronda – first of all, I love Ronda," she said. "We’re very good friends. We’re very good friends to this day so I do want this to get out there. I love her to death but my character is a derivative of coming from The Dungeon. It was something I created after I wrote my book and I realized, man, what I was doing from my very first year of wrestling, it was like Bloodsport before there was ever Bloodsport because I was the only woman trained in the dungeon where I was wrestling men. We were shoot fighting with each other. My grandfather was an amateur wrestling champion of Canada so that was the kind of training in The Dungeon that they went through and there was no ropes. It was just a mat – a mat and some walls. "I always say that I’m Stu Hart’s granddaughter from The Dungeon and I respect the hell out of Ronda. She’s no doubt one of the greatest women to ever compete in MMA. She’s the first person to bring attention and eyes to women in that sport. I loved my matches against her but for me, this is something that is totally different. But the thing is, because I trained with a lot of men, I would never rule out doing an MMA match. I think it would be fun. I would love to beat the s--- out of someone." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Neidhart explicitly explained how much she really enjoyed getting hit, dishing out punishment and even enjoying the taste of blood in her mouth. "And here’s the thing about my character, which is kind of an extension of me in real life is that I really love the taste of blood in my mouth and bruises underneath my clothes," she told OutKick Dropkick. "I love it. It excites me. I just did this rivalry and this storyline with Jaida Parker at NXT and I love that she hit me hard and I love that I hit her hard. "I love that I would come home and I would be like, you know, I’d be scratched up and clawed up and bruised. I mean I had a tooth that was knocked loose and I was like, this is great s---. Jaida said the other day, ‘Nattie really brought out the dog in me.’ And that’s the thing, win or lose, let’s f---ing go. Let me bring out the dog in you because there’s a f---ing dog in me and it’s not a chihuahua." That’s the kind of intensity Roxanne Perez, Faby Apache and La Hiedra need to expect on Night 1 of Triplemania on Friday night. articles.title: Dana White weighs in on Justin Gaethje retirement rumors
articles.summary: Dana White questions whether it's time for Justin Gaethje.
articles.body:
Justin Gaethje has achieved it all in mixed martial arts.

Ranking third all-time in UFC post-fight bonuses despite fighting less than half as many times as the two fighters above him, 'The Highlight' has lived up to his namesake during his time in the octagon. A fun, fan-friendly athlete who is incapable of having a boring fight. The Arizona native could have bowed out of the sport years ago and would still be considered an anomaly. But to cap off an exceptional career in combat sports, Gaethje managed to one-up his two interim titles with undisputed gold in his last outing. The win only added to his legacy, but retirement talk has been closely trailing the 37-year-old for some time.

Likely caused by his own comments, supporters have been preparing for a Justin Gaethje retirement announcement for years. Despite a title-winning performance at the White House, those talks haven't disappeared, leaving many in the dark about Gaethje's UFC future .

Also not knowing what the future holds is Dana White , who has been speaking about his potential return lately. With Gaethje yet to defend his title, White has internalized a potential Ilia Topuria rematch, saying:

"We owe all these guys three fights a year. So guys are always getting offered fights. So, we'll see. And, you know, the big talk is who [Topuria's] going to fight. Is he going to fight Gaethje, or is he going to fight Paddy Pimblett? That is a great problem to have."

Weighing in on Justin Gaethje's potential retirement, Dana White had this to say:

"Not based on his skill level, but based on his last fight and what he accomplished. There's two sides to this coin. If you look at, talk about going out the right way. But he looked incredible. And when you think about how much money is left on the table for him to make. You know, when he still looks good."

articles.title: Delhi HC denies Vinesh Phogat entry to World Championships trials: ‘Not inclined to grant interim exemption’
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to allow wrestler Vinesh Phogat to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to allow wrestler Vinesh Phogat to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships, declining her request for an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI).Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma, in a late-night interim order, said that at this stage, the court was not inclined to grant an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria to allow Phogat to participate in the selection trials on September 14.“To reiterate, the criteria prescribed under the circular dated September 7, 2026 apply uniformly to all athletes. An athlete who has not participated in the prescribed competitions, for whatever reason, would not fall within the eligibility categories specified by respondent no. 1 (WFI),” the court said.The high court passed the order while dismissing an application by Phogat, who has returned from maternity leave, seeking permission to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships.Court flags Phogat’s maternity circumstancesThe court said Phogat’s circumstances relating to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum recovery would require consideration while examining the validity of the policy. However, that does not, at the interim stage, by itself entitle her to a direction permitting her to participate contrary to the eligibility criteria, it added.“Granting such interim relief to the petitioner alone, without first adjudicating upon the policy itself, may consequently result in unequal treatment of similarly situated athletes who are not before this court,” it said.The court added that without expressing any final opinion on the validity of the circular or on the merits of the pending disciplinary proceedings, it was not inclined to grant the interim relief.Phogat challenges September 7 WFI circularPhogat, in her application filed in a pending petition, had also sought a stay on the operation of a September 7 circular issued by the WFI prescribing the eligibility criteria for the selection trials scheduled for September 14 at the Indira Gandhi Stadium here.The fresh application was filed in the main petition in which Phogat has sought formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.In the application, she sought a stay on the circular as it excludes her from participating in the selection trials for the championship scheduled to be held at Astana, Kazakhstan from October 24 to November 1.The WFI circular provides for women’s trials in six Olympic weight categories. Phogat contended that the latest selection framework creates a closed pathway by making eligibility dependent on participation and performance in specified qualifying competitions.The plea said the circular places Phogat in a position where she is excluded not because she has been assessed and found wanting on sporting merit but because she was unable to participate in the particular competitions selected by WFI as gateways to the present selection trials.Court had sought WFI, Centre responseIt said the framework contains no mechanism to account for an athlete who was unable to participate in the prescribed competitions for maternity-related reasons.On September 1, the high court sought the response of WFI and the Centre on Phogat’s plea seeking formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.In the petition, she has sought directions for formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning from maternity, transparent and objectively verifiable selection and nomination processes, and an alternative mechanism for athletes disadvantaged by maternity-related absence.Phogat, who became a mother in July 2025, said upon resuming her wrestling career after childbirth, she was made to re-enter the competitive pathway without any accommodation for the period she was unable to compete due to maternity.The wrestler has also filed another petition seeking quashing of two show cause notices issued to her by the WFI and disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.WFI’s counsel had said they kept the hearing twice but “there has been no show”; a final opportunity was given and the hearing was on September 2.In the plea, Phogat said that the two notices issued to her on May 9 and June 17 were part of a continuing pattern of arbitrary and mala fide action by the WFI, obstructing her return to competitive wrestling after maternity.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I have too much respect”: Why Paulo Costa chose Eddie Hearn as his UFC future reaches a major crossroads
articles.summary: MMA News: Paulo Costa appears to be at an important point in his UFC career. The Brazilian fighter has made a significant change outside the cage by signing wit.
articles.body: Paulo Costa appears to be at an important point in his UFC career. The Brazilian fighter has made a significant change outside the cage by signing with Eddie Hearn, while his future inside the UFC remains uncertain. Costa has explained that the decision came from his respect for Hearn and his belief that the experienced fight business figure can help him move forward. The timing makes the move even more interesting. Costa has also revealed that the UFC rejected multiple requests for a release, despite one fight remaining on his contract. Now, his next step could have major importance.Paulo Costa chose Eddie Hearn because he trusts his experience and believes they can build something bigger togetherCosta's decision to work with Eddie Hearn is rooted in professional respect. The Brazilian previously had Tiki Ghosn handling his management, but he has now moved to Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency.Hearn has built a major reputation in boxing and has also increased his involvement in MMA. His growing group of fighters includes UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall and welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry.For Costa, Hearn's experience was a major reason behind the decision.“I have too much respect for what he’s doing. He’s a great guy, a great professional. I think we’re going to do great things together. I just need to send back the email. I think everything is set up, and I’m so excited. He handles the business very well. He’s a super important person in the fight business. Not only in MMA, but not only in boxing, but he’s coming to MMA right now. I think this is a great acquisition for the MMA community,” Costa said.The partnership also comes despite the well-known tension between Hearn and UFC president Dana White. Costa, however, does not appear concerned that their disagreement will affect his career.“I don’t think so because I don’t put too much attention on this beef between them both. If they have this bad blood between them, it’s not about me, you know? We’re professionals, guys.”Costa's comments show that he views the relationship as a business decision rather than an attempt to take sides in a larger dispute.Paulo Costa’s push for a UFC release explains why his new partnership matters so much right nowThe timing of Costa's management change becomes clearer when his current UFC situation is considered. Costa says he has asked the promotion for his release several times, including just days before his latest comments. The UFC has rejected those requests and wants him to complete at least one more fight.“We already asked to be released, but they refused,” Costa said. “They said, 'No, we're not going to release you. You need to do one more at least.' Actually, I've been asking for this a couple of times. The most recent was like days ago.”Costa was also frustrated after the UFC did not accept his offer to step in following Valentina Shevchenko's withdrawal from UFC 332. He had been pushing to fight for months and believed he could have helped the Salt Lake City card."I'm sad because I think we could have given a much better fight card going on for the Salt Lake City fans," Costa said. "I don't think fans are so happy, I'm not happy, but it's not about me. I've asked to fight since May. I asked them to fight in June, July, August. They told me to wait."Costa last fought at UFC 327 in April, stopping Azamat Murzakanov with a head kick. He now wants a major opportunity at light heavyweight and is also seeking a new UFC contract.That leaves Costa facing an important decision. His next fight could satisfy his remaining UFC obligation while also setting up the next stage of his career. With Hearn now involved, the business side of that future will be closely watched.For Costa, the partnership is not simply about changing managers. It comes at a moment when he is trying to find a clearer path forward, both inside and outside the UFC.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dana White Explains Why UFC Didn’t Re-Sign Michael Page
articles.summary: UFC president Dana White explained why the world’s leading MMA promotion decided not to re-sign Michael Page. Despite having a 5-1 record inside the Octagon,...
articles.body:
UFC president Dana White explained why the world's leading MMA promotion decided not to re-sign Michael Page.

Despite having a 5-1 record inside the Octagon, the UFC made the choice not to re-sign Page, who is now a free agent and able to sign with any other combat sports promotion.

Now, White has opened up about why the promotion didn't bring him back.

UFC Matchmakers Didn't Want Michael Page

Speaking to the media during a scrum ahead of the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn boxing match, White revealed that UFC matchmakers Sean Shelby and Mick Maynard did not want Page back, which is why the promotion let him go.

"Listen, at the end of the day, the matchmakers make the decisions on who stays and who goes, and they didn't want to re-sign him," White said.

Despite the UFC letting go of Page, the middleweight striker should have no problem finding a new home, with Jake Paul of MVP MMA and David Feldman of BKFC already saying they are interested in signing him.

Let's face it, things didn't work out for Page in the UFC.

Despite a 5-1 record, his fights were incredibly dull to watch, so it made sense that he was released and given the opportunity to fight with another promotion.

While Page is obviously a very good fighter who knows how to win fights, he had a problem showing any sort of finishing instincts inside the Octagon, so it didn't make sense for the organization to bring him back for big money just for him to dance his way around opponents en route to decision wins via point fighting.

Still, Page is a really big name in the sport, so he should have no issue finding a new home in short order.

The only hope that fans have is that Page opens up with his striking wherever he goes, because fans are hoping that we get the old version of Page from Bellator MMA, who was knocking out his opponents, not the guy who was prone to just winning on points in the UFC .

articles.title: Gaethje 'vuelve' a UFC Casa Blanca: "Topuria cometió terribles errores emocionales"
articles.standfirst: El ahora campeón del peso ligero ha hablado sobre aquel combate
articles.summary: El ahora campeón del peso ligero ha hablado sobre aquel combate
articles.body: Casi tres meses después de UFC Casa Blanca, celebrado en la noche del 14 de junio, Justin Gaethje (28-5) ha vuelto a hablar sobre su ya histórica victoria sobre Ilia Topuria (17-1). Esta vez, sin embargo, el nuevo campeón indiscutido del peso ligero, ha hablado de cómo de trascendente fue la previa del combate para el desenlace del mismo. 'The Highlight' explica que el 'Matador' cometió "terribles errores emocionales" en los días previos al duelo. Y eso, en su opinión, fue fundamental para que el hispanogeorgiano perdiera su invicto. "No estaba preparado para lo que pasó aquella noche. Es culpa suya. No creía que fuera posible que alguien aguantara tanto tiempo con él en el octágono. Se olvidó de quién era y de lo peligroso que es este deporte", ha declarado Gaethje en una entrevista con una leyenda de la UFC como Demetrious Johnson. Ahora queda por ver cuál es el futuro de ambos pues los dos siguen recuperándose de las lesiones sufridas en aquella batalla celebrada en el jardín sur de la Casa Blanca. Una revancha, como ha explicado Dana White, es una de las opciones que maneja la UFC.

articles.title: Paulo Costa Reveals Why He Signed With Eddie Hearn
articles.summary: UFC light heavyweight contender Paulo Costa explained why he decided to sign with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency.Costa left former manager Tiki Ghosn...
articles.body:
UFC light heavyweight contender Paulo Costa explained why he decided to sign with Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency.

Costa left former manager Tiki Ghosn to join Hearn, a rival of UFC president Dana White, who also has UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall and welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry as part of his stable of MMA fighters, along with all of his boxing stars.

Paulo Costa Explains Signing With Eddie Hearn

Speaking to "The Ariel Helwani Show," Costa explained why he signed with Hearn to manage his MMA career.

"I have too much respect for what he's doing. He's a great guy, a great professional. I think we're going to do great things together. I just need to send back the email. I think everything is set up, and I'm so excited. He handles the business very well. He's a super important person in the fight business. Not only in MMA, but not only in boxing, but he's coming to MMA right now. I think this is a great acquisition for the MMA community," Helwani said (via MMAjunkie.com).

Paulo Costa Not Worried About Hearn-White Feud

While it is clear that Hearn, his manger, and White, his boss, do not like each other, Costa is not worried about that potentially negatively affecting his UFC career.

"I don't think so because I don't put too much attention on this beef between them both. If they have this bad blood between them, it's not about me, you know? We're professionals, guys. I'm just seeing Ryan Garcia fight this guy (Benn), and I think he's still represented by Oscar (De La Hoya), right? And Oscar had that beef against Dana. I think they are very professional, much more than we thought. They can do business together and at the same time talk (expletive) about each other," Costa said.

The Brazilian has not fought since UFC 327 in April, when he knocked out Azamat Murzakanov with a head kick. He is hoping that he gets a light heavyweight title shot in his next fight, but he also wants the UFC to give him a new, big-money contract.

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Champion taunts Briton with an egg during a theatrical news conference
articles.summary: A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and taunted a composed  Conor Benn with a boiled egg before Saturday's WBC welterweight title fight.
articles.body:
A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and even ate a boiled egg - while Briton Conor Benn kept his cool - during a peculiar news conference in Las Vegas.

American Garcia defends his WBC welterweight belt against 29-year-old Benn at the T-Mobile Arena on Saturday.

A fight week which had been relatively quiet finally came to life on Thursday - thanks largely to the unpredictable champion.

While Garcia, 28, bounced between insults, threats and jokes, Benn remained relatively composed.

Benn spoke instead about giving supporters "value for money" and refused to be drawn into many of his rival's taunts.

"All the talking, tweeting, typing and streaming is done - I'm ready to fight," Benn said, while inexplicably wearing a bullet-proof style vest.

Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia

Benn 'dragged down to pits of hell' by weight cut

'Bottling it' - Garcia no-show for first Benn face-off

Garcia is one of boxing's biggest social media stars, with more than 13 million Instagram followers.

He recently appeared on WWE's Monday Night Raw and it did not take long for the news conference to take on a similarly theatrical feel.

Minutes after taking his seat, Garcia reached into a bag, pulled out the egg, calmly peeled it and ate it whole.

"He has a lot of familiarity with eggs so I thought I'd eat some," Garcia said, as his opponent's father - Nigel Benn - shook his head.

It was a reference to Benn's two positive tests for clomifene in 2022 and the WBC's subsequent ruling that elevated consumption of eggs could provide a reasonable explanation.

Adding to the bizarre atmosphere, Garcia said his egg was a bit dry and would benefit from some honey.

Garcia has also served a doping suspension after testing positive for ostarine following his 2024 fight with Devin Haney. Both fighters have denied knowingly taking banned substances.

Before the face-off, security confiscated an egg Garcia had tucked into his pocket, potentially preventing a repeat of last year's incident when Chris Eubank Jr slapped Benn across the face with one.

Benn and Garcia had to be separated at their launch event in New York in July, but there was no repeat this time. As Garcia continued talking, Benn put a finger to his lips, smiled and eventually turned away and left the stage.

Thursday's news conference was held inside Saturday's fight venue, with one section of T-Mobile Arena curtained off for the crowd.

Fans had begun queuing more than an hour before the doors opened. It was not a Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez-sized crowd - and far from anything like the travelling support Ricky Hatton once brought to Las Vegas - but there was still a healthy turnout.

Small pockets of travelling British supporters made themselves heard, while Garcia received a much louder but mixed reception.

Garcia said Benn had "lit a fire" by questioning his Mexican heritage. Benn - who spent 12 years of his childhood living in Majorca - responded by speaking fluently in Spanish.

There was another dose of theatre when WBA 'Super' welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez, disguised with a fake beard, stood among the crowd to ask a question before revealing himself to loud cheers.

Garcia also took aim at Benn's manager Keith Connolly's hairline before turning his attention to the challenger's weight.

Benn has not made the 10st 7lb welterweight limit for more than four years, having fought Chris Eubank Jr twice at middleweight.

Garcia suggested Benn could rehydrate to whatever weight he wanted after Friday's weigh-in but questioned whether his brain would recover sufficiently from the cut.

"[Garcia should] worry about himself," Benn replied. "He seems to have enough problems as it is.

"I don't look at him, I just worry about myself and don't cut corners. We'll see who makes weight tomorrow."

Garcia did eventually acknowledge much of the showmanship was just that.

"All this is noise, I've done my job and I'm the better fighter," he said. "This is fun but we know what to do."

But it did not take him long to slip back into entertainer mode. Even after Benn had left, Garcia remained on stage - flexing, shouting and playing to the crowd.

images.caption: Image caption, Ryan Garcia (left) beat Mario Barrios in February to win the WBC welterweight title

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: 'He lives through me' - why Nigel Benn can't walk away from Conor
articles.summary: Nigel Benn vowed to leave son Conor to plough his own path after he beat Chris Eubank Jr, but the retired world champion is back by his side this week as he prepares to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia.
articles.body:
Nigel Benn had insisted he was stepping away from his son's career for good.

The 10,000-mile trips from Australia - where Nigel is based - were done, and Conor Benn was on his own after his grudge-match win over Chris Eubank Jr.

Yet in the build-up to Conor's WBC welterweight world title challenge against Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas, the 'Dark Destroyer' was by his son's side at the news conference and holding court at their Essex media day - as embedded as ever.

Ask Nigel why and he claims Conor "twisted my arm" into helping with one final hurdle.

"I don't know if he was lying or if he believed it himself," Conor says with a wry smile.

"He lives through me. He goes, 'son, this is my last fight, I'm done.' Then the next one it's, 'son, it's your first defence.' There'll always be something."

Perhaps neither man is ready to cut the cord.

Conor has stepped out of his 62-year-old father's shadow - not by matching the legendary ring achievements, but through the sheer turbulence of his own journey.

Navigating a career-threatening doping case, surviving the ferocious Eubank rivalry and acrimoniously splitting from long-time promoter Eddie Hearn transformed him from 'Nigel's boy' into one of British boxing's most polarising headliners.

Through those storms, Nigel has been there in the trenches.

"It's what Conor thinks and what his dad thinks - that's what it's about, not what everybody else says," Nigel Benn says.

"Everyone's not going to love my son. Everybody didn't love me. But once you get that belt around his waist, we'll go from there."

The storms, sceptics and chasing history

Thirty-six years ago, Nigel flew across the Atlantic as the fiery outsider, tearing through Doug DeWitt in Atlantic City to secure his first world title.

Now, Conor lands on the Las Vegas Strip chasing the exact same milestone. A victory would place the Benns alongside the likes of Floyd and Tracy Harris Patterson, Julio Cesar Chavez and Julio Cesar Chavez Jr and Leon and Cory Spinks in the lineage of father-and-son world champions.

"I've watched him religiously for 10 years put his life on the line," Nigel says. "He's just going from strength to strength, from glory to glory. I see him being victorious. I'm not actually worried whatsoever."

Yet reaching this point has required navigating a volatile road fraught with controversy.

The adverse drug test findings that wiped out two years of Conor's career cast a long shadow, fracturing public perception and leaving unanswered questions that still follow him.

He has always denied doping, a provisional suspension was lifted in November 2024, and he says he has fought throughout his career as "an advocate for clean sport".

Inside the ropes, the jury remains stubbornly out on his talent.

A laboured points victory over Regis Prograis in his last outing did little to convince purists he belongs at the sport's highest echelon.

But Conor cares little for the outside noise or winning over the boxing fraternity.

"To some people, I'll never be good enough," he says. "One day they love you, some day they hate you.

"You keep talking about what other people think, but I don't care. Winning the world title for me, it's personal. If I listen to other people, I wouldn't be where I am."

'Bottling it' - Garcia no-show for first Benn face-off

Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia

Benn 'dragged down to pits of hell' by weight cut

Garcia has walked an equally chaotic path, having served a one-year suspension after testing positive for banned substance ostarine following his win over Devin Haney in 2024.

Both men deny intentionally ever taking performance-enhancing drugs, but away from that issue their showdown is wrapped in the contradictions that define modern boxing.

It will be staged by UFC-backed Zuffa Boxing - following Conor's high-profile split from Hearn - yet featuring the traditional green-and-gold WBC belt on the line, despite Zuffa's public rhetoric about disrupting boxing's old-guard sanctioning bodies.

Social media spats between the fighters have brought plenty of heat, but Conor Benn does not compare it to the raw nature of the Eubank saga, which spilled over into face-to-face fury. An egg was even slapped across Benn's face by Eubank.

"Listen, it's not personal with Ryan. It is personal with Eubank - this ain't no comparison," Conor says.

"One person I wanted to put in hospital; the other one I don't. I just want his title and I want his number one position. I've been at world level for years and for me to claim the number one spot officially is the goal here.

"[Garcia] is like a child. It doesn't bother me. You need people like Ryan in the sport of boxing."

Garcia is proven at the top level and enters as the favourite, bringing blinding hand speed and a fight-ending left hook.

But Nigel Benn believes he has mapped out the exact antidote to Garcia's firepower. He says his son should attack Garcia using suffocating, bobbing aggression - the kind that Nigel used to blow out Iran Barkley in 1990.

"When he goes under pressure, what happens? He falls and his heart doesn't go into it," Nigel says.

"For the first time, [Conor] is actually sitting there listening. He has to be not the destroyer, he has to be the Dark Destroyer. Controlled aggression.

"Don't give him room. Roll under his punches, left hook to the body, left hook to the head. He knows what to do."

The hostile Vegas spotlight, meanwhile, evokes memories of Benn senior's ferocious 1995 battle with Gerald McClellan.

"Everybody had me to be blown out within round three. Exactly the same thing as what they do with Conor," Nigel says. "And I know he's going to prevail."

Win, lose or draw, Nigel insists this time he will walk away for good and let Conor do his own thing.

"I can walk out of that arena, go home, and be with my family, and that's it," Nigel says.

Whether Nigel finally catches that one-way flight back to Sydney is another matter.

If Conor leaves Las Vegas with the WBC belt around his waist, you would not bet against his father being back for defence number one.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn in latest war of words as Teofimo Lopez gatecrashes press conference in disguise
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia accused Conor Benn of struggling to make weight while the Brit insisted he was "not here for a cuddle" as the pair traded blows at their final press conference ahead of Saturday night's WBC welterweight world title fight in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
WBC welterweight champion Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) is set to defend his title for the first time against Benn after clinching the belt against Mario Barrios in February.

Benn (25-1, 14 KOs) meanwhile steps into comfortably the biggest test of his career on the back of April's win over Regis Prograis and his revenge victory over Chris Eubank Jr.

"Just don't cuddle me in here. I didn't come all the way to America for you to cuddle," said Benn.

Both fighters have previously being caught up in controversy with Garcia testing positive for banned substance ostarine in 2024, while in the same year Benn's provisional anti-doping suspension for two failed drugs test in 2022 was lifted.

Garcia, who was a no-show for Wednesday's face-off, was the more animated of the two fighters as he fired insults across the table towards the Brit.

The American's talking continued during the pair's face-off, to which Benn simply raised his finger to his lips before exiting the stage.

"He's going to try real hard, we know that. He's probably going to have to try to resort to some dirty tactics, so we'll be prepared for that," said Garcia.

"And we're just going to do what we do best, which is stay sharp, be ready for everything, and we're prepared, man. We're conditioned 100 percent, and we'll put on a hell of a show, I promise you that."

Benn is making a significant cut in weight having twice fought Eubank Jr at middleweight, his last fight at the 10st 7lb welterweight limit coming against Chris van Heerden in April 2022.

Saturday awaits as the 29-year-old's first-ever world title fight and toughest opponent by some distance.

"I'm not concerned," said Benn. "I don't focus on him and what he does, I focus on what I do. I bring tenacity, ferocity, spite, experience. I've been here before, I've fought in front of 70,000 three times now, on the bounce. So you know I'm here to come and really set the tone from the first round."

Among his barrage of insults, Garcia again questioned Benn's weigh-cut, suggesting he would struggle on the scales the next day.

"I know you're not on weight, because I can see it in your eyes. You ain't on weight," he said. "Hey, you're going to hit that bathtub tonight, or the bike."

Garcia took particular offense to Benn questioning his Mexican heritage, while also firing back at his opponent's father Nigel Benn.

"Come Saturday night when his blood is spilling out his mouth, that will be enough to show him how Mexican I am," he said.

"I heard his dad talking like he was gonna knock me out. Bet he won't. Bet he won't. We can bet whatever too. Your son ain't gonna knock me out. He couldn't even knock out Regis. Your dad ain't right. Your dad lying to you. I hope you know that. Dad lying to you."

Benn insisted Garcia should "worry about himself".

"He seems to have enough problems as it is," he said.

"I don't look at him, I just worry about myself and don't cut corners. We'll see who makes weight tomorrow."

Another twist to their press conference was a surprise appearance by WBA 'Super' welterweight world champion Lopez, who wore a fake beard and introduced himself as 'Jack Hoffman' as he asked a question in the crowd.

articles.title: La UFC duda con Topuria: "¿Peleará contra Gaethje o contra Pimblett?"
articles.standfirst: Dana White, jefe de la compañía, ha revelado que tienen un "bendito problema" para elegir al siguiente rival de 'El Matador'
articles.summary: Dana White, jefe de la compañía, ha revelado que tienen un "bendito problema" para elegir al siguiente rival de 'El Matador'
articles.body: El regreso de Ilia Topuria está cada vez más cerca. Tras perder el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero ante Justin Gaethje en el UFC Casa Blanca, 'El Matador' se tomó un tiempo para sanar las heridas. Ese tiempo ya ha terminado, y una vez ha vuelto al ojo público ya se han visto sus primeros vídeos entrenando. Además, Dana White -jefe de la UFC- ha dicho que el peleador hispanogeorgiano está listo para volver, aunque tienen un gran dilema a la hora de elegir quién será su siguiente rival: La revancha contra Gaethje o un supercombate contra Paddy Pimblett. A priori, el regreso de Topuria apunta a inicios de 2027, ya que necesitará tiempo para entrar en campamento y llegar al 100% después de varias semanas de tranquilidad. Su idea es vengarse de esa dolorosa derrota ante Gaethje lo antes posible, pero el peleador estadounidense no está por la labor de permitirle su redención. La UFC es la que tiene la última palabra, pero ni ellos mismos saben lo que hacer a día de hoy. No hay que olvidar que Paddy Pimblett viene de arrasar a Benoit Saint-Denis y es el archienemigo de Ilia, por lo que también está sobre la mesa enfrentar a ambos en una pelea que sería incluso más mediática que la de Justin por toda la historia que hay detrás entre ambos. "La gran conversación es '¿contra quién va a pelear Topuria en su siguiente pelea?'. ¿Va a pelear contra Gaethje o contra Pimblett? Ese es un gran problema para tener", sentenció en una entrevista con Jim Rome. Lo que está claro es que será una de esas dos opciones, ya que son las más realistas para el regreso de Topuria. En cuestión de legado e importancia, lo normal sería la de Gaethje, ya que le ayudaría a quitar peso a su única derrota y además le permitiría recuperar el cinturón. A Justin no le quedan muchos más combates en la recámara, por lo que puede ser una oportunidad de oro que no se repita en un futuro. Sin embargo, los cantos de sirena de una pelea contra Pimblett también son muy apetecibles. Desde hace años ambos se han atacado públicamente cada vez que han podido, y el odio es real. Son las dos mayores superestrellas del peso ligero, dos de los peleadores más queridos de la UFC y a nivel de negocio sería un éxito asegurado para la compañía. Sea quien sea su rival, la vuelta de Ilia será por todo lo alto, ya que si gana a cualquiera de los dos volverá a aumentar el hype sobre su figura y se entenderá el pasado 14 de junio como una mala noche. Tendrá mucha presión sobre sus hombros y todas las miradas estarán puestas en su actitud y su estado mental tras ese traspiés en la Casa Blanca, pero también es un momento clave para darle una lección al mundo de cómo sobrellevar una derrota. En redes ya lo ha hecho, ahora queda verlo en el octágono.

Ilia Topuria, con sus cinturones de la UFC. AP

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Fight is '100 per cent happening' says Fury's manager as Cardiff emerges as potential venue
articles.summary: Cardiff and Wembley among three potential venues for the all-British super-fight, says Tyson Fury’s manager; Spencer Brown "100 per cent that the fight will happen" with negotiations still ongoing between both camps
articles.body:
The long-awaited British blockbuster fight has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the event with Joshua's team having remained insistent it must take place in the UK.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown is confident the fight will still happen - and on home soil, potentially in December.

"It's inching closer and it looks like it could be the British Boxing Bonanza that we all hoped for taking place in Britain," Brown told Sky Sports .

"Three venues are still under consideration with Cardiff and Wembley still in the running.

"It's looking good, Tyson has been onboard with fighting AJ since the start and he will fight him anywhere.

"November and December are both in play but we like December as an option, everyone would be winding up work for the holidays, it would be the best Christmas party in the world."

Brown added: "I'm 100 per cent that the fight will happen.

"Everyone is still in negotiations, Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren are both onboard but I'm fully confident we can get it done, of course the final say with be with Turki Al-Sheikh, Netflix and SELA but we are on track to getting it done."

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union told Sky Sports in July: "We'd be delighted to host this fight.

"We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location."

images.caption: Image: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury still look on course for their long-awaited meeting

articles.title: Petr Yan gives BRUTAL warning to Merab Dvalishvili ahead of UFC 333 trilogy fight, says “You better get good insurance”
articles.summary: MMA News: Petr Yan has sent a brutal warning to Merab Dvalishvili ahead of their highly anticipated trilogy fight at UFC 333. The UFC bantamweight champion did .
articles.body: Petr Yan has sent a brutal warning to Merab Dvalishvili ahead of their highly anticipated trilogy fight at UFC 333. The UFC bantamweight champion did not hold back while speaking about his plans for their third meeting. Yan told Dvalishvili to get “good insurance” because he intends to break his nose again. The two rivals will meet on October 24 in Abu Dhabi, with the bantamweight title on the line. Their rivalry is tied at 1-1 after two fights, making the upcoming clash a decisive chapter in their story.Petr Yan warns Merab Dvalishvili about his nose ahead of trilogyPetr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili are preparing to settle their rivalry inside the Octagon once again.The fighters will face each other in the co-main event of UFC 333 on October 24, 2026. The event will take place at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Yan will enter the fight as the UFC bantamweight champion.The Russian fighter has already made his intentions clear. He wants to hurt Dvalishvili again, and his latest comments have added more fuel to their rivalry. Yan delivered a direct warning to his opponent ahead of the trilogy.“You better get good insurance before the fight because I’m going to break your nose”, he said via UFC Eurasia.The comment refers to the damage Yan inflicted during their previous meeting. Yan defeated Dvalishvili by unanimous decision at UFC 323 in December 2025. The victory allowed him to reclaim the bantamweight championship.Dvalishvili entered that fight as one of the most dominant fighters in the division. He had won 14 consecutive fights before facing Yan. However, Yan produced a strong performance and handed the Georgian his first loss in several years.The result also levelled their rivalry. Dvalishvili won their first meeting in March 2023. He defeated Yan by unanimous decision after a competitive five-round contest. Yan then responded in their second fight, earning the decision victory and taking the title from Dvalishvili.The trilogy fight will therefore decide who gets the upper hand in their head-to-head record. Dvalishvili has already explained what went wrong for him in the second fight. The former champion believes he was not fully prepared for the contest.Speaking on the ‘Beyond the Win’ podcast, Dvalishvili previously said, “What was hard about last loss, I think | am better than Petr Yan. When I took this fight two months before, 1 knew it was risky because two months is a very short time. When I fought Cory Sandhagen, I took the fight two months after, and it was a very short time.”Dvalishvili also admitted that his demanding preparation affected him. He added, “Against a tough guy like Petr Yan, you need rest and then a good training camp. But I didn’t take rest and I had a hard training camp, which burned me out. No excuses, but I knew it was risky.”With the score tied at 1-1, the stakes could not be higher. And after Yan’s latest nose warning, the trilogy has become even more personal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: International Sports News: Ilia Topuria has opened up about a major change in his mindset after reaching the highest levels of MMA. The UFC star says he no longer depends on ach.
articles.body: Ilia Topuria has opened up about a major change in his mindset after reaching the highest levels of MMA. The UFC star says he no longer depends on achieving career goals to feel happy. Topuria explained that reaching his biggest dreams taught him an important lesson. Success alone was not enough to provide lasting happiness.Instead, he now wants to enjoy the present and make the most of his life. His comments come after a difficult period that saw him suffer the first defeat of his professional MMA career and lose the UFC lightweight title.Ilia Topuria says achieving his dreams was “not enough”Ilia Topuria has changed the way he looks at success. The Spanish-Georgian fighter has already achieved several major goals in his MMA career. He became a UFC champion and established himself as one of the biggest stars in the sport.However, Topuria now says that reaching those goals did not bring the lasting happiness he expected.“So, the thing is that once you achieve your dreams, you realize that it’s not enough. So now I have a completely different mindset. I just try to enjoy the present and enjoy life, and I don’t base my happiness on any goals anymore”, he said via 1win.The comments offer a glimpse into Topuria’s mindset away from the Octagon.For years, Topuria was heavily focused on becoming a champion. His confidence and ambition became a major part of his public image.He eventually reached the top.But his latest comments suggest that he no longer wants his happiness to depend on winning another title or achieving another major career milestone.Topuria’s change in approach comes after a difficult chapter in his fighting career.In June 2026, he suffered the first defeat of his professional MMA career. He faced Justin Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250. He lost his UFC lightweight championship after a fourth-round TKO corner stoppage.The defeat was a major setback for the former champion. Topuria had previously built an unbeaten professional record. He had established himself as one of the most dangerous fighters in the UFC.Despite the loss, Topuria appears to have developed a broader outlook on life.His comments come after his association with 1win. Topuria officially joined the 1win VIP Community on June 2, 2026. The project includes several high-profile athletes and entertainers.Topuria remains a major name in the UFC despite his recent defeat. UFC CEO Dana White has also confirmed that the fighter has recovered and is ready to compete again.The UFC is considering major options for his return. One possibility is an immediate rematch with Gaethje. Another is a highly anticipated fight against Paddy Pimblett.Either matchup would give Topuria another major opportunity.But his latest comments suggest that the outcome may not define his happiness anymore. This is a significant shift for a fighter who built much of his career around chasing the biggest achievements.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 9/11, 25 years later: How Thea Trinidad keeps her father's memory alive through professional wrestling
articles.summary: A quarter century after losing her father Michael in the World Trade Center terrorist attacks, former WWE champion Thea Trinidad still finds solace in their...
articles.body:
On Sept. 13, 2001, Lillian Garcia stood in the center of a WWE ring — alone — with tens of thousands of eyeballs on her at the Compaq Center in Houston. Normally WWE's ring announcer, Garcia had been tasked with a nominal-turned-monumental duty — singing "The Star-Spangled Banner" — two days after the most significant terrorist attack on U.S. soil.

More than 1,600 miles away, in the shadows of the ever-altered New York City skyline, 10-year-old Thea Trinidad watched — as she always did — after experiencing an upheaval most do at some point in their life, but few as suddenly as her.

"That one's specifically always stuck out to me," Trinidad, a former WWE champion who performed under the alias Zelina Vega, tells Uncrowned. "I remember that one specifically, I saw all of the wrestlers get really emotional and seeing Lillian, still I always tell her: 'Yours is still my favorite to hear.'

"It just felt like, in that moment, the thing that I loved most was kind of shining a light on my dad. In a way, it kind of felt like it was just for 9/11, and it felt like it was just for those people. And I think in a weird way, it was important for us to feel that, because everyone else just felt like you were a thing, like a spectacle. You were someone to look at. You almost felt like you were the circus animal, and you were like, 'Oh, look, they dealt with that,' or, 'Oh, look, her dad died.' It just felt like wrestling was the thing that I've always felt seen in."

Trinidad's father, Michael Angel Trinidad, was a telecommunications analyst at Cantor Fitzgerald, working on the 103rd floor in the North Tower at the World Trade Center on Sept. 11th, 2001. Home from school awaiting a doctor's appointment, Trinidad was present when her father made one of hundreds, maybe thousands of gut-wrenching phone calls that morning.

"Because they were divorced at the time, my mom didn't even know that he worked at the World Trade Center," Trinidad recalls. "My brother and I knew because he would take us there all the time. And I remember because we would think, like, 'Oh my God, this is such a weird feeling,' because you'd feel the building sway. As you were standing there, you felt it kind of swaying. So us as kids, we would think, 'Wow, this is so cool.'

"At first when we saw it, I thought it was like some horror movie or something, you know?Or some action movie, or something that was happening that couldn't be real. He had called and just told her, 'I'm calling to say goodbye because I don't think I'm going to make it out.' She was so taken aback by that. I think at that point, once I understood that it was my dad that was actually in the buildings, I felt like it was like a weird out-of-body experience, where I saw everything, and I couldn't move. I couldn't speak. Everything in my body just felt frozen."

The phone call, which Trindad remembers lasting from 9:04 to 9:14 a.m., came 18 minutes after American Airlines Flight 11 struck the building, notably below Cantor Fitzgerald's offices. The fire and wreckage below, combined with the rising smoke, made escape near-impossible. There was a confession of profound love from Michael Trinidad to his family — and instructions to Thea's stepfather: "Please be a father to my kids. I know they love you, so please be there for them like I would."

At 10:28 a.m. ET, the North Tower collapsed. Michael Trinidad was dead at the age of 33.

"From then there were a lot of things going on at once, that I just feel like, as a 10-year-old, I couldn't really process that well," she says. "Because even after we kind of figured that he obviously didn't make it, I would still — because I would go with him every weekend — I still packed my bags thinking that he was going to come. So I think, even psychologically, it took some time before I understood what was going on."

In the aftermath of an unthinkable loss, Trinidad managed to pull purpose out of the wreckage and refused to let tragedy define the trajectory of her life. First, she found Camp Haze, a summer camp founded in 2002 for children who lost a family member in the attacks, named for Scott Hazelcorn, a 29-year-old broker for Cantor Fitzgerald who died in the World Trade Center.

"I think I'm very good at putting a mask on and pretending like everything is okay and everything's totally fine, you know?" Trinidad says. "You need to have an outlet that, when it either does explode, or hopefully before it even gets to that point, you have an outlet, a safe place to actually feel like you are heard, accepted, and understood, because I think that's all anybody really wants is someone who understands them.

"For the longest time, I was the 9/11 kid. People would act so weird around me in school, especially when it came to that time. They'd be like, 'Oh, we just saw her reading names on the news,' like during the 9/11 thing. My own friends didn't even know how to talk to me. So, I think I just needed people who also just understood me."

After Camp Haze — where Trinidad eventually became a counselor — the Queens native homed in on the place where she always felt seen: her memories at Madison Square Garden with her father and brother.

"I remember around 15 years old is probably when it really hit me," Trinidad says. "[My dad] showed me a match between Rey Mysterio and Eddie Guerrero back in, like, 1997. It was Halloween Havoc , and I never forgot it. I remember seeing that thinking, 'I want to do that.' He was really the only one at that time that was super supportive of it. I knew that it was his dream, too, because he was an amateur wrestler in high school — I still have his wrestling trophies — he wanted to do it professionally, but with three jobs and a wife and kids, that just wasn't going to happen.

"So after everything, I said I'm going to do this for him, but I'm going to do this for me too, and live our dreams together."

By 2011, Trinidad was wrestling for TNA and spent the better part of the next decade wrestling on the independent circuit, using the name Rosita. In 2017, Trinidad made her way to WWE as Zelina Vega. During Trinidad's time with WWE she rose from primarily managing Andrade to winning the inaugural Queen of the Ring tournament, becoming a Women's Tag Team Champion and Women's United States Champion.

Most importantly, Trinidad was able to create relationships that helped foster her late father's dream, even beyond the ring. Trinidad was cast to play AJ Lee in 2019's "Fighting With My Family," a biopic of WWE star Paige that was produced by Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson's Seven Bucks Productions.

"It's just crazy sometimes, even when I look back, The Rock was his favorite wrestler, and the fact that I ended up meeting him and working with him and becoming very close to him, to the point where Dwayne and his daughter got to go and visit my dad's name, at the 9/11 Memorial, is still mind-blowing to me," Trinidad said. "I'm like, that's so crazy. The Rock knows your name. That's still wild."

Trinidad, along with her husband Tom Budgen — aka pro-wrestler Malakai Black — were released from WWE earlier this year. It was a significant blow that put Trinidad in a position she had been in before, most notably after her father's passing, 25 years ago. With her mother and brother struggling, Trinidad put off her own reconciliation with the tragedy to become the rock for those closest to her.

"A lot of things just kind of plummeted this year for me, and I think that's where it goes into survival mode, and it starts to kick in, and I'm like, 'OK, where do we go next?'" she says. "'OK, we're going to pick back up streaming. OK, we're going to explore these other opportunities that you've never been able to.' Korea, I've never been there. Japan, I haven't been there in a while. It allows me to not feel like there's nowhere else to go.

"Whenever I'm at a really, really low point, I'm the person that takes care of my family. They depend on me. So I have to be that strong anchor for them too, because [if] something happens to me, that means something happens to them, and I can't allow that. So that's where I guess the protective side comes in."

Trinidad, now using the ring-name Xelina, made her official wrestling return at House of Glory earlier this month as well as appearing at PROGRESS wrestling in the UK. Trinidad also rattled off TNA, AEW and Stardom as other potential opportunities in this new chapter of her career.

"It almost feels like a second chance to explore that other side of what my character could be and what I can be as a professional wrestler," Trinidad says. "Especially working with different people, but also giving me a second chance to live that dream for my dad and making sure that dream doesn't die."

As with most things in life, the more time that passes the less impactful moments — even those as reality-breaking as the 9/11 attacks — feel, especially from those who aren't as close to it as Trinidad. Anniversaries eventually turn into afterthoughts, moments bound for history books and entering the national discourse on nice, round numbers.

"Although some people may not feel like it's directly affecting their family or themselves, it's something that we as a country went through together, no matter what," Trinidad says. "You can't really let something like that go. They always say, '9/11, never forget,' and it's because I think the biggest thing for me that came out of that was how much we all came together. No matter what the differences were, all of us came together at once to be there for each other as a country. I remember how that felt, and I don't think I've ever felt that really since."

As Trinidad continues to keep her father's memory alive through professional wrestling, she has some help, too. Trinidad's fans still visit the 9/11 Memorial and take pictures next to Michael's name, and Trinidad herself will occasionally draw the old New York City skyline on her wrestling sneakers. Trinidad even recalled a fan's sign at a show that proclaimed: "Michael Trinidad will always have the best seat in the house."

"I still feel like I have a world title that I want to bring him," Trinidad says. "I still feel like there's just so much more of me to give. I will do this until my bones break and make sure that I can't do it anymore."

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Conor Benn & Ryan Garcia both make weight for WBC title fight
articles.summary: Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia both comfortably make the welterweight limit for their WBC title fight despite concerns at how they would fare on the scales.
articles.body:
Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia both comfortably made the welterweight limit for their WBC title fight despite concerns at how they would fare on the scales.

Briton Benn, 29, weighed in at 10st 6lb (66kg) for Saturday's bout - half a pound heavier than the champion.

The official weigh-in took place behind closed doors at the UFC Apex on Friday, in front of about 50 members of the media, before a ceremonial event later in the day which will be open to the public.

Garcia has won 25 of his 28 professional contests, including 20 knockout victories, with two defeats and one no-contest. Benn has 25 wins - 14 by knockout - and one loss, and is fighting for his first world title.

American Garcia, 28, won the WBC belt with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making his first defence against Benn.

Eggs, insults & a champion with a fake beard - Garcia and Benn face off

Why Nigel Benn can't walk away from Conor

Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia

Much of the build-up this week has centred on how Benn would cope with returning to the 10st 7lb welterweight limit for the first time in more than four years.

His two fights against Chris Eubank Jr were both at middleweight, with Benn weighing 11st 2lb (71kg) for the first and 11st 5lb (72kg) for the rematch. For his win over Regis Prograis in April, Benn weighed 10st 10lb (69kg).

He has already said he will vacate the title and move back up in weight if he beats Garcia.

Benn had looked increasingly gaunt and drawn during fight week and told BBC Sport the cut had taken him to the "pits of hell" .

But Benn smiled as his weight was announced and looked in good shape, surprising several observers who had expected the effects of the cut to be far more visible.

A handful of undercard fighters weighed in after Benn while Garcia was still nowhere to be seen, prompting questions about whether the Californian was having difficulties making the limit.

Garcia has had problems on the scales before. He weighed more than three pounds over the light-welterweight limit before his fight against Devin Haney in 2024.

There was no such drama this time. Garcia sprinted towards the scales about 10 minutes after Benn and also looked at ease as he comfortably made weight.

The weight is particularly significant because of the contrasting styles.

Benn relies heavily on aggression, explosiveness and sustained pressure, while Garcia is a fast and dangerous counter-puncher who is comfortable catching opponents as they come forward.

Any draining effects of the cut could therefore leave Benn more vulnerable to Garcia's speed and powerful left hook, while also raising questions over whether the Briton can maintain his usual intensity over 12 rounds.

With no rehydration clause in place, Benn said he could weigh as much as 12st 7lb (80kg) by the time he steps into the ring on Saturday.

He is still an underdog against Garcia - a fighter with greater amateur pedigree and a more accomplished professional resume - but Benn's size and physical pressure could become one of his biggest advantages.

articles.title: Why is Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn a superfight? Because boxing isn't meritocratic
articles.summary: Neither Garcia nor Benn is considered one of boxing's best pound-for-pound fighters. They may not even be the two best welterweights in the world. Yet when t...
articles.body:
"You can play football, you can play basketball, you can play baseball, but you don't play boxing."

We have all heard some variation of that adage, used to convey the unforgiving nature of the sport. But in 2026, how true does it really ring?

Last Saturday — and not for the first time — I watched Dave Allen enter the ring massively overweight for his fight with Thomas Carty in front of more than 83,000 fans in a sold-out national stadium. Ryan Garcia has admitted to smoking cannabis and drinking alcohol heavily during training camp for his infamous 2024 bout against Devin Haney.

Both men looked like they were playing boxing.

Allen has spent much of the past decade arriving out of shape — and, by his own admission, barely training for some fights — yet the sport has continued to provide him with significant paydays . Hundreds of other boxers are more talented and hardworking, yet they will never be rewarded with even one of the dozen opportunities that have come Allen's way.

Garcia appeared to be abusing substances in the weeks before a major championship fight, but it did little damage to his career or reputation — at least as far as the recreational substances were concerned.

Perhaps you can play boxing from time to time.

Garcia and his opponent this Saturday, WBC welterweight title challenger Conor Benn, perfectly illustrate how boxing may be the only sport in which the highest earners are not necessarily its most talented or accomplished competitors, and its biggest opportunities routinely fall at the feet of those who have done the least to deserve them.

Garcia and Benn have one more thing in common: failed drug tests.

Benn twice returned adverse analytical findings for the fertility drug clomiphene in 2022 but never received a ban. Less than a fortnight after Garcia recorded the biggest victory of his career over Haney, it emerged that he had tested positive for ostarine.

In other sports, they may have been sidelined for years. But not in boxing, no.

Garcia received a lenient 12-month suspension and his victory over Haney was overturned to a no-contest. Considering top-level boxers rarely fight more than twice a year, a one-year suspension is essentially a one-fight ban in practice.

Benn's drawn-out case ended when an independent National Anti-Doping Panel concluded that it was "not comfortably satisfied" that he had committed an anti-doping rule violation. Would a little-known fighter, without the same financial and legal firepower, have emerged from that process with the same outcome?

But boxing's biggest stars were never going to be adequately punished for their crimes.

Garcia's one-year absence from the sport felt almost inconsequential. Throughout it, he attended major boxing events, faced off with prospective opponents and publicly discussed his return. There was no sense that his place in boxing had been taken away.

And most disappointingly of all, there was no shame.

In a meritocratic sport, a fighter returning from a drug suspension might have been required to prove himself again. Not in boxing. Before Garcia even completed his suspension, it was announced that he'd return in a world title fight against Rolando "Rolly" Romero.

Garcia vs. Romero was a historically dreadful contest , and Garcia lost.

He had returned from a drug suspension, performed abysmally, and been beaten in a world title fight. Only in boxing could his reward be another world title opportunity.

This time, Garcia did strike gold. He impressed in dethroning Mario Barrios and finally legitimized a career that had endured its fair share of turbulence.

Now, Barrios was arguably the weakest champion in the sport, but Garcia could not control that. You can only beat the man put in front of you. If boxing had decided to make Barrios a champion in a division as historic and prestigious as welterweight, then so be it.

But Garcia was not Barrios' mandatory challenger, nor was he even a deserving contender. He received the opportunity because he was the most lucrative opponent available. It was another example of boxing prioritizing popularity over merit — and few fighters have benefited more from that tendency than Garcia.

Benn is now Garcia's mandatory challenger.

Simply put: Benn is a major star, and his former promoter, Matchroom, did an excellent job of advancing his interests. Last year, the son of Hall of Famer Nigel Benn went 1-1 across two enormous middleweight fights with Chris Eubank Jr. By the end of it, Matchroom had successfully petitioned for Benn to be installed as the WBC's No. 1 contender at 147 pounds and, eventually, its mandatory challenger — despite not having fought at welterweight since April 2022 and not having recorded a major victory in the division.

Souleymane Cissokho won a WBC final eliminator in May 2025 against another proven contender, Egidijus Kavaliauskas. He should have been next. But, as so often happens in boxing, he was pushed aside to make way for the bigger commercial attraction.

Garcia's career has carried him from one major fight to the next. Knockout losses, racist and homophobic online rantings , a failed drug test and dreadful performances — none of them have prevented enormous opportunities from arriving.

Benn's career was built on the foundation of his father's name. As Nigel's son, a raw novice was afforded the rare luxury of developing beneath the brightest lights until an inherited rivalry with Eubank delivered a pair of eight-figure paydays.

Now one of boxing's biggest stars, he is set to earn an eight-figure purse for a fourth consecutive fight — and still nobody can be certain that Benn belongs anywhere near the sport's elite.

Neither Garcia nor Benn is considered one of boxing's leading pound-for-pound fighters . They may not even be the two best welterweights in the world. But when they step through the ropes on Saturday night, millions of eyes will be watching because it is a genuine superfight. That's boxing in 2026.

articles.title: Video: Noche UFC full card faceoffs with Silva vs. Delgado, McMillen slap
articles.summary: The entire Noche UFC card headlined by Jean Silva vs. Jose Delgado had final faceoffs at ceremonial weigh-ins.
articles.body:
UFC Fight Night 288 ceremonial weigh-ins are in the books, and the fighters came face-to-face one final time before Saturday's event.

The weigh-ins took place at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz., which hosts the card ( Paramount+ ).

UFC Fight Night 288 is built around a five-round featherweight bout bout Jean Silva (17-3 MMA, 6-1 UFC) and Jose Delgado (12-2 MMA, 4-1 UFC). It also features former Mexican champions Brandon Moreno (23-10-2 MMA, 11-6-2 UFC) and Alexa Grasso (13-2 MMA, 8-1 UFC) scheduled for key bouts in their respective weight classes.

Check out the video above to see highlights from Friday's ceremonial weigh-in staredowns, including all 13 scheduled bouts at UFC Fight Night 288.
